trades.headline: Sell Likely and Corum at their peak for a 2027 1st plus Godwin — Fannin already covers your TE1 slot for free
trades.summary: Isaiah Likely and Blake Corum are both producing well above their roles right now; cash them in for a future first-round pick and a cheap buy-low receiver while Harold Fannin Jr. is already playing well enough to absorb the TE1 job.

give: Isaiah Likely is at 16.7 ppg against a 12.0 projection (1.39x) on a 77% snap share and 25% target share
Blake Corum is at 11.6 ppg against an 8.4 projection (1.38x) on just a 33% snap share and 6% target share
Both are up on the 30-day trend (Likely +11%, Corum +36%), the window to sell before the market corrects
get: Chris Godwin Jr. is at 6.2 ppg against a 10.2 projection (0.61x) while still playing 84% of snaps
His role hasn't shrunk, the production has: a 16% target share is modest but his snap count says he's not buried
The 2027 1st (Early) is priced at 4,903 — this league's own first-round picks have hit at a 4% bust rate
you: Harold Fannin Jr. is already rostered and outproducing his own role (87% snap, 20% target share), so he fills TE1 at no cost
You bank a projected-early 2027 first and add a buy-low WR for bench depth without touching your starting lineup
them: Elite 11 QB camp is 1-10 and thin at RB/TE — Corum and Likely are immediate roster upgrades at both spots
The deal is priced even by value, so they're not giving up the pick at a discount, just spending future equity on present need
experts: The Giants signed Likely to a 3-year, $40M deal this offseason expecting him featured in the passing game (SI, Giants.com)
Corum remains the clear change-of-pace back behind an extended Kyren Williams in Los Angeles, with limited room to grow (SI Rams preview)
Godwin's target share has been squeezed by Tampa Bay's younger receivers, but he's still playing a full complement of snaps (Yardbarker)

risks: Fannin was also flagged as a sell-high candidate by the numbers — his own price could cool before you've gotten a full season from him
A rebuilding 1-10 team spending a future 1st on two complementary vets instead of hoarding picks is the shakier part of this for them

trades.headline: Flip two hot, inconsistently-used pieces (Burden, Fannin) for a true TE1 in Trey McBride plus a QB lottery ticket
trades.summary: Luther Burden III and Harold Fannin Jr. are both outproducing modest roles and trending up in value; package them for McBride, who solves your thin TE spot with a workhorse instead of a hot streak.

give: Luther Burden III is at 15.0 ppg against a 12.6 projection (1.19x) on only a 59% snap share and 22% target share
Harold Fannin Jr. is at 12.2 ppg against a 10.8 projection (1.14x), up 31% in value over 30 days — sell before that cools
Burden's role has been inconsistent all season, repeatedly out-produced in snaps by teammates in Chicago's receiver room
get: Trey McBride is a true workhorse at 90% snaps and a 29% target share — the volume, not a hot streak, drives his production
Kyler Murray is a near-free speculative stash while hurt; if he resets as a starter later, the cost here was minimal
you: Trey McBride starts immediately at TE and Tetairoa McMillan moves into the lineup, a clean two-starter upgrade
You turn two bench-tier, trend-dependent assets into the best tight end available on the market
them: Mother Theresa's child is thin at QB/RB and deep at TE/WR — they can afford to move their TE1 for immediate help at your excess positions
Burden and Fannin are productive right now, which is exactly the sales pitch a thin-at-the-position team wants to hear
experts: McBride became the first TE with back-to-back 100-catch seasons, and Arizona has publicly refused Denver's trade inquiry for him (CBS Sports, Heavy.com)
Burden has been inconsistent in Chicago's pass game, including a Week-3 game where he was 'again out-produced by Kalif Raymond' (NBC Sports)
Murray was released by Arizona, signed a one-year deal in Minnesota, then suffered a Grade 2 strain in early November — a real but cheap gamble (Fox News, Heavy.com)

risks: Murray is currently out and Minnesota's QB competition behind him remains unsettled, so this piece of the deal may never pay off
Arizona's public refusal to trade McBride means this partner would be moving a true cornerstone, not just a hot name — may be a tough sell

trades.headline: Sell Jonah Coleman at his statistical peak for a workhorse in Jonathan Taylor plus a Kyle Pitts flier
trades.summary: Jonah Coleman's per-game output is running well ahead of a still-timeshare role in Denver; cash him in now with a far-off pick for Jonathan Taylor, whose full workload hasn't changed even though his price has dropped, plus Kyle Pitts as a flier.

give: Jonah Coleman is at 16.3 ppg against a 9.8 projection (1.65x) on a 57% snap share and just 14.7 touches a game, up 85% in value over 30 days
His role is real and growing as J.K. Dobbins fades, but it's still a timeshare — his goal-line work is contested, and that per-game pace is well ahead of what a part-time role sustains
A 2029 1st is three drafts away and priced at 1,936 — distant equity you can turn into production now
get: Jonathan Taylor is at 16.4 ppg against an 18.7 projection (0.88x) but still logged a 79.2% snap share in Week 8, his role intact
His value is down 33% over 30 days on quieter box scores, not a lost job — a textbook buy-low
Kyle Pitts is a secondary piece at 92% of his projection, a cheap add at a position you're thin at
you: Jonathan Taylor steps directly into your RB1 spot, addressing your thinnest position with a true workhorse
You lock in Coleman's peak price instead of betting his current pace holds once Denver's backfield picture settles
them: Your trade partner is 9-2 and thin at TE/WR, deep at QB/RB — they can spend a spare runner and banked pick on need
Coleman still carries name value from his rookie-draft hype even with his current role buried, which is what makes him sellable
experts: Coleman has established himself as Denver's lead back as J.K. Dobbins has faded (13 yards on 7 carries in Week 8, 4 carries in Week 9), per Draftsharks
He posted a career-high 58-of-75 snap share in his biggest game, but his goal-line role is still contested — Dobbins scored from the 1-yard line in a recent game
PFF logged Taylor at a 79.2% offensive snap share in Week 8, his largest share since Week 3, despite a quieter box score (Draftsharks)
Atlanta has franchise-tagged Pitts for 2026 and GM Ian Cunningham says the team will 'listen' on calls, but no trade has happened — he remains in Atlanta's rotation (AJC)

risks: Coleman's role is trending the right way for Denver, not fading — if he keeps the job outright this could look like selling too early
If Indianapolis leans further into a run-committee in blowout wins, Taylor's touches could keep shrinking even with his snap share intact
Pitts carries real trade-rumor noise; if Atlanta deals him mid-season his target share could shift in a way you can't predict yet

trades.headline: Cash in a hot backup QB and a bench RB for a buy-low rookie WR, with a cheap speculative QB flier thrown in
trades.summary: J.J. McCarthy is producing well as the Giants' new starter, but he's pure backup value on your deep QB bench; package him and Kenny Gainwell for Denzel Boston's buy-low role plus a speculative add in Carson Beck.

give: J.J. McCarthy is at 13.7 ppg against a 12.0 projection (1.14x) and has won the Giants' starting job outright, up 13% in value over 30 days
Kenny Gainwell is at 7.4 ppg against an 8.3 projection but trending up 28% in value on touchdown-fueled weeks, not role growth
get: Denzel Boston is at 90% snaps and a 20% target share, the Browns' clear No. 1 receiving option, down 15% in value on recent quiet games

Carson Beck took over as Arizona's starter after Kyler Murray's release, but is currently out and the exact cause isn't confirmed — treat this piece as a cheap, speculative flier rather than a settled buy-low
you: You're already deep at QB with Caleb Williams, Drake Maye and Tyler Shough, so McCarthy is pure sell-high depth
Gainwell is buried behind Tampa Bay's lead back; neither piece you're sending starts for you
them: Katseye Dad is 3-8 and thin at WR/TE, deep at RB/QB — a rebuild-mode team collecting a real starting-caliber backup QB and a complementary RB
McCarthy's hot recent stretch is the exact selling point a thin-at-QB rebuilder wants to hear
experts: McCarthy was named the Giants' starter over Jameis Winston in October and played through a hip injury in a Week-11 win over Philadelphia (ABC7NY)
Boston was listed as the Browns' No. 1 WR on the early depth chart and has repeatedly led the team in receiving (NBC Sports)

Beck had moved up to Arizona's QB1 job before his most recent absence; the cause of his current out designation hasn't been reported clearly, so this piece of the deal is a lottery ticket, not a core value add

risks: If the Giants keep winning with McCarthy, you'll be watching a legitimate starter produce for someone else
Boston's rookie role could cool if Cleveland's passing volume dips in the final stretch of the season
Beck's current situation in Arizona is unresolved — if he's hurt or has lost the job outright, that piece of the trade is worth little

trades.headline: Sell Tank Dell's touchdown spike and a buried bench WR for a still-featured Metcalf in a red-zone drought
trades.summary: Tank Dell's big game is an outlier off a long injury layoff, and Savion Williams is firmly the Packers' No. 3 option; turn both into DK Metcalf, whose role hasn't shrunk even though his scoring has.

give: Tank Dell is at 10.7 ppg against a 5.0 projection (2.14x), driven by his first touchdown in 687 days, two games off a long knee injury
Savion Williams is a clear No. 3 receiver in Green Bay behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, with no touchdowns yet in 2026
get: DK Metcalf is at 90% snaps and a 22% target share, tied for Pittsburgh's team lead, despite a 0.81x performance and -27% 30-day trend
He's gone back-to-back games without a red-zone target, per CBS Sports — a touchdown drought, not a lost role
you: Neither Dell nor Williams starts for you now; Metcalf is a straight swap into bench WR depth with a much higher ceiling if the red-zone looks turn into scores
them: 28AllDay is 7-4 and thin at WR/RB — Dell's explosive return game and Williams's depth both address an immediate need for a team trying to win now
experts: Dell caught a 63-yard touchdown from C.J. Stroud on November 8, his first score in 687 days and just his second game back from a long knee injury (Newsweek, ABC13)
Williams is described as 'a clear No. 3 receiver' behind Watson and Golden after returning from his own injury (AtoZ Sports)
Metcalf has gone consecutive games without a red-zone target despite a team-leading target share in Pittsburgh (CBS Sports)

risks: Dell's touchdown could be the start of real volume, not just a one-game outlier, which would make this look early
If Pittsburgh's offense keeps starving Metcalf in the red zone for scheme reasons rather than bad luck, the touchdowns may not come back
